column4: Options. The word alone makes people nervous, and honestly, it should. An option can turn a small bet into a rocket, or into a puff of smoke, like the one this guy is watching. Same tool, two completely different endings. Today we learn what makes it grow, what makes it vaporize, and the rules that keep you on the rocket side.

First, the superpower and the trap: leverage. Look at the kid on the lever. A tiny push lifts a giant boulder. Options work the same way. A small amount of money controls a much bigger position, so a move in the stock gets multiplied. That is amazing when you are right. But leverage does not care when you are wrong. It multiplies losses just as hard. Same lever, both directions.

Here is the part that catches beginners. Watch the two paths on the chart. One option catches the move and rips higher, the green rocket line. The other one just fades to zero. When you buy an option, the most you can lose is the premium, the price you paid. That sounds safe, until you realize the whole premium really can go to zero. Grow big, or vaporize completely. There is not a lot in between.

And here is the sneaky enemy: time. Every option has a deadline, an expiration date. Look at the hourglass and that melting ice cube. That is your premium, quietly melting a little every single day. It is called time decay. The clock is always running, even when the stock does nothing. Wait too long, and the option can melt away before the move ever shows up. Time is not on your side here.

column4: Okay, your call. I give you a setup: an option, and what the stock does before the deadline. You tell me, did it grow, or did it vaporize? Think about direction and time. Tap your answer.

Five questions. Show me you respect the leverage and the clock.

So that is options in one lesson. Leverage cuts both ways, the premium is the most you can lose, and time decay is always melting the clock. The golden rule? Learn stocks first, practice on paper, and never bet money you cannot afford to see vaporize.
